newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: High call rates keep Sri Lanka forex market low.
newsitem.headline: High call rates keep Sri Lanka forex market low.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee barely moved against the dollar in early Wednesday trade due to high call money rates and a lack of imports, dealers said.
At 0500 GMT the rupee was at its opening level of 58.25 to the dollar. The rupee closed at 58.32 on Tuesday.
"We have seen hardly any demand for dollars due to a lack of imports and high call rates, which have led to some selling of the currency," said an ANZ Grindlays dealer.
The Central Bank leaving the dollar-ruepe exchange rate unchanged despite he greenback moving up overseas, also led to banks selling the U.S. unit, they said.
The Central Bank's buying and selling rates remained at 58.2541 and 59.4309.
"The Central Bank's action has encouraged banks to sell dollars and generate rupees, which should help the tight money situation," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Call rates were at 19 percent after opening at 17 percent, dealers said.

"Money is tight due to cumulative impact of quarterly tax payments, holidays when there are high cash withdrawals, banks covering imports with dollars from the Central Bank and weekly auctions of 500 million rupees worth of treasury bonds," said a Sampath Bank dealer.
